prose: 404 Media chronicles a weekend trend: people using AI to reverse-engineer and replace the software on consumer devices, from swapping smart-TV operating systems for debloated AI-written ones, to reviving bricked Lululemon mirrors, turning smart picture frames into AI calendars, and stripping ads out of baby monitors. It is vibe coding pointed at existing proprietary software: decompiling, cloning features, and installing open-source replacements, partly plagiarism machine, partly users taking back control of devices locked down, ad-laden, or abandoned by their makers. Open-source politics researcher Mike Nolan tells 404 Media that engineers keep saying SaaS is dying as a business model because recreating functionality has become so easy, though he questions whether the clones will be maintained reliably enough for companies to adopt.
highlights: Trend: AI reverse-engineering of TVs, picture frames, baby monitors, bricked Lululemon mirrors
Goal is usually debloating, de-advertising, or resurrecting abandoned devices
Mix of decompiling, cloning, vibe coding, and open-source replacement
Mike Nolan: 'software-as-a-service is dying as a business model'
Caveat: maintenance burden may limit clone reliability and adoption
Framed as users reclaiming control from arbitrary lockdown and surveillance
